newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Aug 1.
newsitem.headline: Australian Stocks to Watch Today - Aug 1.

text.p: Some Australian stocks to watch this morning:

Australia's Foster's Brewing Group Ltd said its 40 percent stake in Canada's Molson Breweries was a core asset and dismissed speculation it would sell out. Foster's chief executive Ted Kunkel issued the statement after Foster's partner in the Canadian brewer, Molson Cos Ltd, was reported to have raised the prospect of Foster's exit.

James Hardie told its shareholders at its annual meeting in Melbourne on Thursday it saw a significantly higher profit in 1997/98, but it expected a smaller proportion of franking credits to apply to its dividend payments in future years. It also said it was looking at entering the Japanese housing market through Japanese house builder, Sekisui Chemical Co.

J.B. Were Stockbroking has put a sell recommendation on Hills Motorway Ltd, the operator of Sydney's M2 motorway, and has estimated a fair value range of A$1.35 to A$1.66 a share, market sources said on Friday. A Were report had estimated the M2 would generate long term average daily traffic volumes of about 49,800 vehicles, well below Hills' prospectus forecasts of 72,000 by the end of 1998.

Papua New Guinea oil producer and explorer Oil Search Ltd said on Thursday that its share of crude oil output from the Kutubu oilfield in the nation's highlands region fell to 540,550 barrels in the calendar 1997 second quarter from 616,500 barrels in the first quarter.

Gold miner St Barbara Mines Ltd said it was disappointed with a drop in production and rise in cash costs for the the fourth quarter to June 30. Production came in at 605,423 ounces for the quarter at a cash operating cost of A$526 an ounce, compared with 635,423 ounces at a cash cost of A$403 an ounce in the preceding quarter.

QNI is expected to release later on Friday an independent report into its A$2.3 billion merger plan with South African miner Gencor Ltd's nickel arm. The report is expected to make a judgement on whether the merger is fair and reasonable and provide more details about the deal.
Email is due to hold its annual meeting late on Friday morning.
